The atlas

One body of work, several collections.

The project is being built in layers so the interface never gets ahead of the evidence underneath it.

This is a working research build, not a finished retrospective.

The radio catalogue is mature. Authored-work discovery is now substantial. Teaching, video, social, transcription, deduplication, and thematic synthesis are still growing.

What is intentionally unfinished

The first text-comparison pass has confirmed at least 5 redundant source records across near-identical republication groups, so 312 writing source records currently imply no more than 307 distinct works. That is still an upper bound, not a final count: strong-overlap candidates remain separate until manual review. Beit Simcha dates and displayed titles are fully enriched. Facebook results remain discovery-only when direct content is login-gated.

Current teaching context

The Beit Simcha Adult Education Academy currently identifies seven Sam-led or Sam-co-led programs in this research pass: Zohar, the Book of Samuel Project, Torah Study, Adult B’nai Mitzvah, Introductory Judaism, The Beginning of Zohar, and This Is Judaism. Program records provide context but are not counted as discrete works.

Emerging intellectual landscape

The atlas will connect recurring ideas, not just files.

These are research directions suggested by the corpus already located, not final thematic findings.

Torah in contemporary life

Classical text used as a live lens on ordinary choices, public questions, character, and community.

Research strand

Justice & moral agency

What Jewish ethics require when ideals meet imperfect human institutions.

Research strand

Israel, Zionism & peoplehood

Radio, sermons, travel reports, identity, security, continuity, war, and peace.

Research strand

Freedom, responsibility & choice

Exodus, covenant, obligation, personal enslavement, and spiritual freedom.

Research strand

Resilience, memory & loss

Jewish memory lived forward through grief, communal trauma, survival, and recovery.

Research strand

Pluralism & Jewish community

Conversation across movements, identities, institutions, and generations.

Research strand

Research method

Source first. Interpretation later.

The atlas is designed so later synthesis can always be traced back to the evidence supporting it.

01 · LOCATE

Find the public record

Identify first-party archives, durable source URLs, recordings, posts, and republications.

02 · NORMALIZE

Make it searchable

Standardize dates, titles, people, source type, link state, and provenance.

03 · REVIEW

Read or listen at source

Promote a record only when its actual text, transcript, or audio has been reviewed.

04 · CONNECT

Map ideas across decades

Build thematic links, recurring arguments, teaching patterns, and evidence-backed synthesis.

Project scope

The archive centers Samuel M. Cohon’s public work, teaching, broadcasting, congregational writing, scholarship, and Jewish communal life. It is an intellectual and archival portrait, not a general clipping file.
